title: Project Overview
description: Start with README.md to understand Hinata's purpose as a warm, emotionally expressive AI companion for Telegram. This document covers the feature set including natural conversations, long-term memory, multiple personalities, dynamic moods, and a relationship system, all powered by Groq's free API. It also provides the project structure map and a quick-start installation guide that sets the context for every file you will encounter on this tour.

title: Application Boot & Configuration
description: The app.py script is the process-level entry point — it configures rotating-file logging, initializes the SQLAlchemy database engine, calls bot.py's create_application to wire up the PTB Application, registers signal handlers for graceful shutdown, and starts polling. The config.py module provides Pydantic-based settings loaded from environment variables (bot token, Groq API key, database URL), making all runtime dependencies explicit at startup.

title: Bot Wiring & Core Constants
description: The bot.py module is the central wiring hub — its create_application function instantiates all AI engines (MoodEngine, PersonalityEngine, RelationshipEngine, PromptBuilder), registers every command and message handler, and assembles them into the PTB Application instance. The constants.py module feeds static values (file paths, timeouts, mood/personality defaults) into nearly every other module, making it the most-referenced file in the project with a fan-in of 11.

title: Database Foundation & ORM Models
description: The database layer is built on SQLAlchemy with an async SQLite engine. database.py manages the engine lifecycle — initialization, session provisioning via async context manager, and cleanup on shutdown. The models.py module defines five ORM entities: User (Telegram identity, relationship score, mood, personality), Conversation (chat messages with role and timestamp), Memory (persistent user memories with importance scoring), Preference (per-user settings for emoji level, reply length, personality), and Setting (global key-value app configuration). All models inherit from a shared Base class and carry audit timestamps.

title: Data Service Layer
description: Building on the database models, three service modules provide the CRUD operations that the rest of the application depends on. user_service.py handles user lookup-or-creation by Telegram ID and preference management. chat_service.py persists and retrieves conversation history in chronological order. memory_manager.py provides long-term memory CRUD with bounded importance scores, type-filtered queries, and bulk deletion — enabling the bot to remember user facts across sessions.

title: Message Processing Pipeline
description: The message_handler.py file is the heart of the chat flow, orchestrating a sequential pipeline: input validation, user lookup or creation, conversation context building, AI inference via GroqClient, relationship tracking updates, memory extraction, response cleaning, and reply delivery. It is guarded by utils/rate_limit.py (sliding-window per-user throttling with a decorator API) and utils/validators.py (message length bounds, input sanitization, prompt injection detection via regex patterns). This handler has a fan-out of 12, tying with bot.py as the project's most-connected module.
languageLesson: Python decorators are used here as middleware: rate_limit_decorator wraps PTB handler functions, checking a sliding-window timestamp list before allowing the handler to proceed. The decorator factory pattern lets you configure limits per-handler.

title: LLM Integration & Response Processing
description: The GroqClient (ai/groq_client.py) wraps HTTP communication with the Groq API, providing async chat completion with retry logic, exponential backoff, and HTTP 429 rate-limit handling. The context_builder.py module queries recent conversation messages from the database and formats them into a context string for the LLM prompt. After generation, response_cleaner.py strips unwanted patterns, truncates at sentence boundaries, splits long messages for Telegram's length limit, and escapes MarkdownV2 special characters while preserving intentional formatting.

title: Emotional Intelligence Engines
description: Four engines work together to give Hinata its emotionally expressive personality. PersonalityEngine loads 8 distinct personas (Sweet, Calm, Smart, Gamer, etc.) from a JSON file, each specifying vocabulary, humor level, emoji frequency, and reply length. MoodEngine selects moods based on time of day and random chance, providing mood-specific behavior instructions. RelationshipEngine tracks user relationship levels through a threshold-based scoring system, adjusting interaction warmth and greetings. PromptBuilder composes all of these — personality, mood, relationship instructions, conversation history, and detected language — into a coherent system prompt for the LLM.

title: Personality & Mood Configuration Data
description: These JSON configuration files define the raw data that drives Hinata's emotional expression. personalities.json defines 8 personas with structured traits (vocabulary tier, humor level, emoji frequency, greeting style, energy level). moods.json defines 9 emotional states with energy modifiers, tone settings, and emoji preferences. templates.json contains the core system prompt with slot-filling placeholders that the PromptBuilder resolves at runtime, plus greeting variants and fallback responses. The templates depend on both moods and personalities, making these three files a tightly coupled data triad.

title: User Commands, Admin & Error Handling
description: The command_handler.py implements all user-facing Telegram slash commands — /start, /help, /about, /ping, /version, /settings, /personality, /mood, /memory, /forget, and /reset — each with full interaction flows that call into the service layer. The admin_handler.py provides an owner-guarded /admin command with subcommands for stats, broadcast, maintenance mode, logs, database backup, and user listing. The error_handler catches unhandled exceptions globally, logs full tracebacks, and sends a generic error message to the user, ensuring the bot never crashes silently.
